$comment: PERMISSIONS PROFILE FOR THE LAYER 2 WEEKLY AUTONOMOUS RUN. Loaded by
tools/terminal_next_weekly.cmd via tools/weekly_claude_child.cmd as:
claude -p --settings <this file> --add-dir <docs worktree> --permission-prompts none
DENY-BY-DEFAULT. `allow` lists command PREFIXES; anything unmatched would have prompted,
and --permission-prompts none turns a prompt nobody can answer into a denial.
DENY BEATS ALLOW, and that is the load-bearing property: --settings is ADDITIVE to the
operator's own settings, so `allow` could be widened from outside this file. `deny` cannot.
MEASURED 2026-09-14 against Claude Code 2.1.270 - a Bash prefix rule matches at WHOLE-TOKEN
boundaries. `Bash(python -m pytest tests/test_:*)` did NOT match a real named-file run (probed
headless: DENIED), and `Bash(railway ssh --service web "/opt/...` cannot match inside a quoted
argument. The only rules that DO match are `pytest tests/:*` - which also matches the bare
`pytest tests/` that reached 18 GB and was OOM-killed - and `railway ssh --service web:*`,
which is an unrestricted shell on the production pod. The rule that works is the rule that
permits the hazard, so BOTH constraints live in tools/weekly_exec.py instead and the raw forms
are DENIED below. Rail: tests/test_weekly_exec.py.
git is allowed beyond fetch/status/log/merge-base/rebase/push - add/commit/diff/show too -
because section 3 of the prompt pre-authorizes MERGES, and a unit that cannot commit cannot
complete one. The destructive verbs (reset, checkout, stash, clean, worktree remove) are DENIED.
curl is host-pinned to the Discord webhook prefix. The capability exists to satisfy the brief;
it is unusable in practice because UCT_TERMINAL_NEXT_WEBHOOK is cleared in a child process
before claude is launched, so the model never holds the token.
TRANSITIVE TRUST, STATED ON PURPOSE: allow-listing `python tools/<x>.py` grants whatever that
tool does, including any subprocess it starts. flag_ledger_audit.py shells `railway variables`,
which is DENIED to the model directly and reachable through the tool. Accepted because that
tool is read-only by construction; NOT a licence to allow-list a tool that writes.
There is deliberately no `defaultMode` key: this CLI's --permission-mode takes
acceptEdits|auto|bypassPermissions|manual|dontAsk|plan and none of them is 'default'. Rather
than ship a key whose value was never verified, the deny-by-default behaviour is carried by
--permission-prompts none, which WAS verified by probe.
